xna-type.name: ArtistCollection
xna-type.summary: The collection of all artists in the media library.
xna-type.syntax: public sealed class ArtistCollection : IEnumerable<Artist>, IEnumerable
xna-type.remarks: The ArtistCollection class provides access to all artists in the device's media library. Use the MediaLibrary.Artists property to obtain the artist collection. The ArtistCollection does not immediately instantiate instances of all artists in the collection. Instead, individual Artist objects are created each time an artist is accessed through the collection's Item indexer.

property.name: Count
property.summary: Gets the number of Artist objects in the ArtistCollection.
property.value: Number of Artist objects in this ArtistCollection.

property.name: IsDisposed
property.summary: Gets a value indicating whether the object is disposed.
property.value: true if the object is disposed; false otherwise.

property.name: Item
property.summary: Gets the Artist at the specified index in the ArtistCollection.
property.value: A new Artist representing the artist at the specified index in this ArtistCollection.
property.remarks: Each call returns a new Artist instance. Artist resources such as the song and album collections for that artist are cached in each Artist instance. Retrieving and maintaining references to multiple instances of the same artist, and accessing the Songs or Albums collections on each of those instances, creates multiple copies of the song or album collections.

method.name: Dispose
method.summary: Immediately releases the unmanaged resources used by this object.

overload.summary: Immediately releases the unmanaged resources used by this object.

method.name: Finalize
method.summary: Releases unmanaged resources and performs other cleanup operations before garbage collection reclaims the ArtistCollection.

overload.summary: Releases unmanaged resources and performs other cleanup operations before garbage collection reclaims the ArtistCollection.
overload.remarks: This method overrides Finalize System.Object.Finalize . Application code should not call this method. The object's Finalize method is automatically invoked during garbage collection, unless a call to the GC.SuppressFinalize method has disabled finalization by the garbage collector. For more information, see Finalize Methods and Destructors , Cleaning Up Unmanaged Resources , and Overriding the Finalize Method .

method.name: GetEnumerator
method.summary: Returns an enumerator that iterates through the ArtistCollection.

overload.summary: Returns an enumerator that iterates through the ArtistCollection.
overload.remarks: The foreach statement of the C# language ( for each in C++, For Each in Visual Basic) hides the complexity of enumerators. Therefore, using foreach instead of directly manipulating the enumerator is recommended. Enumerators can be used to read the data in the collection, but they cannot be used to modify the underlying collection. Initially, the enumerator is positioned before the first element in the collection. At this position, Current is undefined. You must call MoveNext to advance the enumerator to the first element of the collection before reading the value of Current . Current returns the same object until MoveNext is called. MoveNext sets Current to the next element. If MoveNext passes the end of the collection, the enumerator is positioned after the last element in the collection and MoveNext returns false. When the enumerator is at this position, subsequent calls to MoveNext also return false. If the last call to MoveNext returned false, Current is undefined. You cannot set Current to the first element of the collection again; you must create a new enumerator instance instead. An enumerator remains valid as long as the collection remains unchanged. If changes are made to the collection, such as adding, modifying, or deleting elements, the enumerator is irrecoverably invalidated and its behavior is undefined. The enumerator does not have exclusive access to the collection; enumerating through a collection is intrinsically not a thread-safe procedure. To guarantee thread safety during enumeration, you can lock the collection during the entire enumeration. To allow the collection to be accessed by multiple threads for reading and writing, you must implement your own synchronization. This method is an O(1) operation.
